arxiv-2012-03605.title: On the characterization of butterfly and multi-loop hysteresis behavior
arxiv-2012-03605.creator: M.A. Vasquez-Beltran, B. Jayawardhana, R. Peletier
arxiv-2012-03605.description: Abstract While it is widely used to represent hysteresis phenomena with unidirectional-oriented loops, we study in this paper the use of Preisach operator for describing hysteresis behavior with multidirectional-oriented loops. This complex hysteresis behavior is commonly found in advanced materials, such as, shape-memory alloys or piezoelectric materials, that are used for high-precision sensor and actuator systems.

arxiv-2101-00586.title: Spin Polarization Induced by Inhomogeneous Dynamical Condensate
arxiv-2101-00586.creator: Ziyue Wang 1, Pengfei Zhuang 1
arxiv-2101-00586.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ziyue Wang 1, Pengfei Zhuang 1. The role of dynamical chiral condensate in spin polarization is investigated in a kinetic theory framework. Transport equations for quark matter are derived in the mean-field approximation for the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model. The dynamical condensate carries part of the energy momentum tensor (EMT) and the angular momentum tensor (AMT), the conservation of EMT and AMT can be proved from the kinetic equations as required by the symmetry.

arxiv-2105-10608.title: Analytic normal mode frequencies for N N identical particles: The microscopic dynamics underlying the emergence and stability of excitation gaps from BCS to unitarity
arxiv-2105-10608.creator: D. K. Watson University of Oklahoma Homer L. Dodge Department of Physics and Astronomy Norman, OK 73019
arxiv-2105-10608.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by D. K. Watson University of Oklahoma Homer L. Dodge Department of Physics and Astronomy Norman, OK 73019. The frequencies of the analytic normal modes for N N identical particles are studied as a function of system parameters from the weakly interacting BCS regime to the strongly interacting unitary regime. The normal modes were obtained previously from a first-order L = 0 L=0 group theoretic solution of a three-dimensional Hamiltonian with a general two-body interaction for confined, identical particles.

arxiv-2403-03584.title: Speed limits to the growth of Krylov complexity in open quantum systems
arxiv-2403-03584.creator: Aranya Bhattacharya, Pingal Pratyush Nath, Himanshu Sahu
arxiv-2403-03584.description: Abstract Recently, the propagation of information through quantum many-body systems, developed to study quantum chaos, have found many application from black holes to disordered spin systems. Among other quantitative tools, Krylov complexity has been explored as a diagnostic tool for information scrambling in quantum many-body systems.

arxiv-2505-14275.title: Application of Deep Learning to the Classification of Stokes Profiles: From the Quiet Sun to Sunspots Facilities: DKIST ( Rimmele et al. 2020 ; de Wijn et al. 2022 ) , Hinode ( Kosugi et al. 2007 ; Tsuneta et al. 2008 ; Lites et al. 2013 ) , GREGOR ( Schmidt et al. 2012 ; Kleint et al. 2020 ; Doming
arxiv-2505-14275.creator: Ryan J. Campbell, M. Mathioudakis, Carlos Quintero Noda, P. H. Keys, D. Orozco Suárez
arxiv-2505-14275.description: Abstract The morphology of circular polarisation profiles from solar spectropolarimetric observations encode information about the magnetic field strength, inclination, and line-of-sight velocity gradients. Previous studies used manual methods or unsupervised machine learning (ML) to classify the shapes of circular polarisation profiles. We trained a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) comparing classifications with unsupervised ML.

arxiv-2507-18655.title: Part Segmentation of Human Meshes via Multi-View Human Parsing
arxiv-2507-18655.creator: James Dickens, Kamyar Hamad
arxiv-2507-18655.description: Abstract Recent advances in point cloud deep learning have led to models that achieve high per-part labeling accuracy on large-scale point clouds, using only the raw geometry of unordered point sets. In parallel, the field of human parsing focuses on predicting body part and clothing/accessory labels from images.

arxiv-2508-20541.title: Machine-learning based particle-flow algorithm in CMS
arxiv-2508-20541.description: Abstract The particle-flow (PF) algorithm provides a global event description by reconstructing final-state particles and is central to event reconstruction in CMS. Recently, end-to-end machine learning (ML) approaches have been proposed to directly optimize physical quantities of interest and to leverage heterogeneous computing architectures.

britannica-1911-veins-geology.title: Veins (geology) (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)

britannica-1911-veins-geology.description: Article 'Veins (geology)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. They may have originated in many different ways and present a. great variety of forms and structures. We may classify them in three groups: (i.) veins of igneous rock, (ii.) of sedimentary, and (iii.) of minerals deposited by water or by gases.

pmc-11643005.title: Overweight Prevalence Changes Before and After COVID-19 in Spain: The PESCA Program Longitudinal Outcomes 2018–2021
pmc-11643005.creator: F. Zarate-Osuna, C. Quesada-González, A. G. Zapico, M. González-Gross
pmc-11643005.description: Background: Overweight prevalence in Spain reached critical levels before the COVID-19 pandemic, which likely exacerbated this issue. The PESCA (Programa Escolar de Salud Cardio-vascular) program is a multicomponent school-based intervention, launched in 2018 with the aim of tackling this health problem and reducing overweight rates in youth.

pmc-12478028.title: Challenges and methodological considerations for research on the role of sleep stage transitions in altered affective processing
pmc-12478028.creator: Maia ten Brink, Haimei Yu, Jin-Xiao Zhang, Sylvia D Kreibig, Rachel Manber, Andrea Goldstein-Piekarski, James J Gross
pmc-12478028.description: Frequent sleep stage transitions and abnormal sleep stage distribution are features of sleep disorders, including insomnia, sleep apnea, and narcolepsy, and have been associated with altered affective processing, including mood disorders. Research on the role of sleep stage transitions is nascent, and mixed operationalizations abound.

pmc-12546938.title: Linear and weakly nonlinear stability analyses of Darcy Bénard convection with feedback control
pmc-12546938.creator: P. G. Siddheshwar, Vinit Vinod Revankar, M. S. Jagadeesh Kumar
pmc-12546938.description: In this paper, the effect of feedback control on the criterion for the onset of Darcy–Bénard convection \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\left( \textrm{DBC}\right)$$\end{document} in a horizontal Boussinesq Newtonian fluid is studied theoretically. The bounding isothermal lower and upper surfaces are considered to be rigid.

pmc-12570456.title: Single-cell landscape of mouse lungs exposed to intermittent hypoxia
pmc-12570456.creator: Pengdou Zheng, Lingling Wang, Xiaoyan Zhu, Zhenyu Mao, Fengqin Zhang, Guisha Zi, Lixiang Chen, Huiguo Liu, Ling Zhou, Wei Liu
pmc-12570456.description: BackgroundObstructive sleep apnea–hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) is a prevalent respiratory disorder characterized by intermittent hypoxia (IH), which promotes pulmonary complications. However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying IH-induced lung remodeling remain poorly understood.MethodsWe performed comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis of lung tissue from IH-exposed mice (GSE145435). Computational approaches were used to characterize cellular heterogeneity, transcriptional programs, and cell-cell interactions.

pmc-12578733.title: Impact of pet ownership in early childhood at ages 1 and 4–5 years on mental health at ages 7–8: findings from the INMA project
pmc-12578733.creator: Llúcia González, Mònica Guxens, Blanca Sarzo, Ainara Andiarena, Loreto Santa-Marina, Adonina Tardón, Jordi Julvez, Cristina Rodríguez-Dehli, Marisa Rebagliato, Marisa Estarlich
pmc-12578733.description: BackgroundWe aimed to explore associations between the presence of pets at one and 4–5 years of age with internalizing and externalizing problems at 7–8 years.MethodsParticipants comprised 1893 families from the INfancia y Medio Ambiente (INMA) project. Information was collected on the presence of (1) any pet, (2) dogs, (3) cats, (4) birds or (5) other animals.

pmc-12586673.title: A deep hybrid inception network model with entropy based attention for automated iron ore image characterization
pmc-12586673.creator: Shama Firdaus, Shamama Anwar, Subrajeet Mohapatra
pmc-12586673.description: Iron ores are an important mineral resource for the industrial development of an economy. Grading of ores is an important task involved at different stages of ore processing. The present study focuses on the grading of iron ores and uses reflected light microscopic iron ore image dataset. The ores were included from different mines of Singhbhum Craton of Eastern India.

pmc-12611812.title: Montmorillonite-based essential oil carrier and its effects on non-target species: an environmental perspective on its risk assessment
pmc-12611812.creator: Sofia Machado, Catarina Ganilho, Tatiana Andreani, Rose Marie O. F. Sousa, Artur Ribeiro, Ruth Pereira
pmc-12611812.description: IntroductionEssential oils (EO), rich in bioactive metabolites with biocidal activity, present great potential for agricultural applications as new biopesticides. However, their high volatility and sensitivity to environmental conditions limits their application. To address these limitations, nanotechnology-based formulations have been developed, incorporating EO into natural clays such as montmorillonite (MMT).

pmc-13064756.title: Autonomy and compulsory care in the Netherlands
pmc-13064756.creator: Esther Nauta, Gerben Meynen
pmc-13064756.description: This chapter discusses the Dutch Law on Compulsory Mental Healthcare (Wvggz), which aims to strengthen the autonomy of patients with severe mental disorders by recognizing that coercive measures can be used not only to prevent harm, but also to restore autonomy. This approach challenges the traditional notion that coercive measures inherently undermine autonomy.

pmc-13425315.title: Recycling Potential of SLS-Degraded PA12 Powder for Melt-Based Manufacturing: Insights Resulting from the Advanced Crystallization Modeling
pmc-13425315.creator: Roman Svoboda, Jakub Vlachynský, David Jaška, Jana Machotová, Jana Navrátilová
pmc-13425315.description: Selective laser sintering (SLS) of polyamide 12 (PA12) generates large quantities of thermally aged powder whose altered crystallization behavior limits its complete reuse in additive manufacturing. In the present study, the feasibility of repurposing SLS-degraded PA12 powder in conventional melt-processing techniques is investigated.
